entries.text: `EnhancedSCDType2Processor.process_scd_changes` now writes its changes to the database. It expires the current version of a changed history-tracking dimension row (`IsCurrent` 0 and `EndDate` set to the new `EffectiveDate`, TPC-DI clause 4.4.1.3), inserts the new version and new natural keys, and overwrites the non-SCD attribute columns and `BatchID` in place on rows whose only changes are non-SCD. Before this it only counted them. Statements use bound parameters and run in one transaction; the returned counts are the rows the database reports as affected, and `scd_type2_changes` counts one per superseded key so that the new, SCD, updated and unchanged counts add up to `records_processed`. A failed read of the current dimension or a failed `BEGIN` now aborts the run before any write instead of treating the table as empty. Table and column names are checked against an allow-list before any SQL is built, a caller-owned transaction is protected with a SAVEPOINT (the run fails closed on connections without SAVEPOINT support, such as DuckDB), and non-SCD attributes that are NULL on both sides no longer count as changed. A run that fails and rolls back reports zero for the new, SCD and updated counts, and a failed `COMMIT` is rolled back so the transaction is never left open. The processor is not called by the TPC-DI ETL pipeline, so published TPC-DI results are unchanged.
